Modern.tagline: A modern small fashion label. Textile-led.

Modern.mission: To make womenswear from real woven textiles that improve with wear, sourced from heritage mills.
Modern.vision: A fashion label whose garments are documented in family wardrobes decades after delivery.
coreValues: Considered — heritage-mill textiles are the foundation.
Modern — small catalog with textile discipline.
Warm — garments are designed for long wear.
Specific — every mill is credited.
Modern.brandNameRationale: Weft and Warp are the two foundational structural threads of woven fabric — the lateral and longitudinal threads on a loom. Paired with an ampersand they ground the brand entirely in textile-trade vocabulary. Two-noun & paired naming follows the considered-modern fashion school (Toile & Tweed, Selvedge register).
Modern.manifesto: Most modern fashion brands chase seasonal trends and trade in synthetic blends. We started Weft & Warp because the actual best clothing is made from real woven textiles from heritage mills — fabrics that age, soften, and improve with wear. The brand is the textile choice; the garment is the result.
Modern.industrySummary: Womenswear has split between fast-fashion volume and a small considered-modern cohort. The opening is for a small label that explicitly positions on heritage-mill textiles with documented mill relationships and garments designed for decade-long wear.
Modern.competitorLandscape: Khaite (khaite.com) plays the closest peer in considered-modern womenswear at premium. Toteme (toteme.com) holds the considered-minimal womenswear peer slot. Studio Nicholson (studionicholson.com) sits in the considered-modern peer position. Imogene + Willie (imogeneandwillie.com) plays the heritage-craft peer reference. We belong alongside Khaite with a sharper textile-mill focus.
Modern.positioningStatement: Weft & Warp is a small modern womenswear label using heritage-mill woven textiles for garments designed to age into the fabric.
Modern.positioningRationale: We compete on textile sourcing and garment longevity. Heritage mills are credited. Garments are designed to wear in over years.

Luxury.vision: An atelier whose 100-year-old commissions are still worn and re-tailored by the granddaughters of the original clients.

Luxury.brandNameRationale: Atelier Vassallo uses the Atelier + Italian surname convention common to heritage Italian fashion ateliers (Atelier Versace, Atelier Mendini, Atelier Cesari historical tradition). Vassallo is a real Italian surname with a craft-trade register. The Atelier prefix places the brand firmly in the heritage Italian fashion atelier tradition.
Luxury.manifesto: Atelier Vassallo was founded in Milan in 1962 and remains in continuous family operation. The atelier produces custom commissions for individual clients — measured, fitted, and finished by the principal designer and a small team of permanent dressmakers. The client roster grows by referral. Many clients are the daughters and granddaughters of original clients.
Luxury.industrySummary: Heritage Italian fashion ateliers are rare and dominated by luxury conglomerates. There is space for a small independent atelier operating in the heritage tradition with by-appointment custom commissions and multi-generational client relationships.

Schiaparelli (schiaparelli.com) sits in the heritage couture peer position. Valentino Couture (valentino.com) plays the heritage Italian couture peer reference. We belong with the small heritage Italian ateliers translated to a private practice.
Luxury.positioningStatement: A small Milan-based fashion atelier producing custom womenswear by appointment for individual clients, with the principal on every commission.
Luxury.positioningRationale: We do not extend the atelier. The principal is on every commission. Client relationships span multiple generations of the client family.

Minimal.brandNameRationale: Three words, one process. Cut & Sew is the literal description of how clothing gets made before the brand layer is applied. The name puts the work in the brand position. Honest. Old. Unpretentious.
Minimal.industrySummary: Most fashion brands lead with the look. We lead with the make. The customer wants clothing that was actually made by someone, not assembled. The category needs a brand that says so plainly.
Minimal.competitorLandscape: Many small fashion brands operate in this aesthetic space. None have claimed the language as bluntly. The closest spirit is Margiela's blank-tab tradition, applied to a smaller, quieter line.
Minimal.positioningStatement: Clothing cut and sewn, made to last, sold without marketing.

Minimal.brandNameRationale: Selvedge is the self-finished edge of woven fabric — single textile-trade word, deeply specific. Single-word naming follows the apothecary-minimal school translated to fashion (Khaite, Toteme register).
Minimal.manifesto: Most fashion brands write a paragraph where one word would do. They name a feeling, a place, a season, a mood. We make clothes you wear. The brand is the thing in your hand. Hold it up. If you would wear it, take it home. That is the brief.
Minimal.industrySummary: Quiet luxury is a crowded shelf now. The opening underneath it is louder and simpler: a brand that strips the language back further than COS or Uniqlo and lets the garment do the talking. The customer is tired of being sold to.
Minimal.competitorLandscape: COS (cos.com) is the reference for plain modern dressing. Uniqlo (uniqlo.com) holds the everyday slot. Asket (asket.com) owns the permanent collection idea. We sit a step further out than Asket, with even less language around the product.
Minimal.positioning: WEAR is a clothing brand for people who are done reading about clothes. The collection is small, the names are descriptive, and the only marketing is the garment itself. Buy the shirt. Wear the shirt.
Minimal.targetAudience: Adults 28 to 50 who have bought their last trend piece. They know their measurements, they re-buy what works, and they read the label more than the campaign. Most of them got here after a few expensive mistakes.
Minimal.personality: Plainspoken. Patient. Unbothered by what is happening on the other side of the shop window. Says one thing and lets it sit.
Minimal.voiceAndTone: Captions are the product. 'White shirt. Cotton. Made in Portugal.' That is the post. No setup, no story, no hashtag.

Minimal.vision: A womenswear brand whose tenth-anniversary catalog is the same six pieces as its first.

typography.rationale: Inter scales clean across digital. The serif handles printed B2B documentation and licensing contracts.

customSections.title: What it doesn't do
customSections.body: No consumer brand of our own. No D2C ecommerce. No celebrity partnerships. No retail stores. The firm sells through B2B sourcing, not Instagram.

Corporate.brandDescription: Apparel manufacturing and licensing for brands at scale.
Corporate.mission: Retailers and brand licensees want production partners with operational discipline and a design-led understanding of the category. We sit in the middle, more design-aware than the giants, more reliable than the boutiques.
Corporate.vision: The vendors compete on production reliability, quality control, and operational scale.
coreValues: Reliable — the same answer this Tuesday and next.
Capable — a core principle the brand operates by.
Direct — we say what we mean without softening it.
Steady — a core principle the brand operates by.
Professional — a core principle the brand operates by.
Corporate.scope:
Heritage Apparel Partners works across:
• Production at scale
• Quality controls built in
• One partner across categories

Corporate.tagline: Garment manufacturing, sourcing, and distribution for North American brands.
Corporate.brandNameRationale: Burlow is a surname pulled from a 1940s pattern-maker who never got famous. Apparel Group is what the entity is. Together it sounds like a holding company that has been around longer than it has, which is the point. The name signals trade buyer, not consumer.
Corporate.manifesto: We do not run a fashion brand. We run the factory floor, the sourcing trips, the QA lines, and the freight schedules that brands depend on. Our customer is the merchandiser, the production lead, the founder who needs a partner that picks up the phone in February and is still on the line in November.
Corporate.industrySummary: Apparel sourcing is fragmented and increasingly nearshore. Buyers want shorter lead times, smaller MOQs, and a partner who can absorb the operational load. The vendors who win are the ones who feel less like factories and more like extensions of the brand team.
Corporate.competitorLandscape: Li & Fung (lifung.com) remains the global reference. Suuchi (suuchi.com) has built the tech-forward story. Indigenous Designs (indigenousdesigns.com) holds the ethical mid-market. We sit in the practical middle: serious operations, North American footprint, no PR theater.
Corporate.positioning: Burlow Apparel Group is a manufacturing and distribution partner for emerging and mid-market apparel brands. We handle sourcing, production, QA, and warehousing so brand teams can focus on design and customer.
Corporate.targetAudience: Founders and production leads at apparel brands doing $2M to $50M in annual revenue. They have outgrown their first factory and need a partner who can scale with them without losing the craft conversation.
Corporate.personality: Senior. Operational. Speaks in production calendars and landed cost. Comfortable in the back of house. Does not need to be in the campaign.
Corporate.voiceAndTone: Direct, specific, and unembellished. We talk about CMT pricing, fabric mills, and shipping windows. Decks have numbers, not adjectives.

messagingPillars.title: Sourcing
messagingPillars.body: Vetted mill and trim relationships across Portugal, Peru, and the U.S. Southeast. Fabric library and sample turnaround inside 14 days. Tariff and origin documentation handled in-house.

messagingPillars.title: Production
messagingPillars.body: MOQs from 250 units. In-line QA on every run. Production planning shared with brand teams in a working document, not a black box.

messagingPillars.title: Distribution
messagingPillars.body: 3PL partners in Atlanta and Reno. Direct-to-retail and direct-to-consumer fulfillment under one purchase order. Returns processing and refurb included.

Corporate.logoDirection: Burlow set in a serif with a small caps Apparel Group beneath it on a single rule. A trade-buyer mark, not a consumer mark. Used on invoices, contracts, and trade-show booths.
Corporate.colorPalette: Charcoal #2A2A2A primary, oat #E8E1D2 secondary, factory red #B23A2D as a single accent. Restrained, industrial, slightly American.
Corporate.typography: A traditional serif for the wordmark, a clean grotesque for documents and tables. Numbers tabular, hierarchy disciplined.
Corporate.brandDescription: We do not run a fashion brand.
Corporate.mission: We do not run a fashion brand. We run the factory floor, the sourcing trips, the QA lines, and the freight schedules that brands depend on.
Corporate.vision: Our customer is the merchandiser, the production lead, the founder who needs a partner that picks up the phone in February and is still on the line in November.

Corporate.brandDescription: Eastwell Apparel Holdings operates a portfolio of apparel brands across casual, denim, outerwear, and footwear categories.
Corporate.scope:
Eastwell Apparel Holdings works across:
• Multi-brand apparel manufacturing and operations
• Shared global supply chain and factory relationships
• Retail distribution to department stores and specialty channels
• Direct-to-consumer e-commerce infrastructure for the portfolio
• Annual investor and operator reporting
Corporate.mission: To provide a serious operating platform for mid-tier apparel brands that want to keep their identity and outsource the operations.
Corporate.vision: An apparel operator whose portfolio brands grow under their own names because the supply chain and retail infrastructure are shared.
coreValues: Senior — partners deal with partners.
Operational — supply chain runs on schedule.
Reliable — predictable production across brands.
Discreet — brand relationships stay private.
Corporate.brandNameRationale: Eastwell is a real English place-name with a heritage trade register. Apparel Holdings follows the multi-brand operator naming convention used in apparel (PVH Corp, VF Corporation, Tapestry Inc structure). The pair reads as an institutional operator with multi-brand portfolio scale.
Corporate.manifesto: Eastwell Apparel Holdings owns and operates a portfolio of apparel brands. Each brand retains its identity, design leadership, and customer relationships; we operate the shared global supply chain, retail distribution, and back office. The buyer is an apparel brand founder considering sale, a department store seeking single-vendor brand relationships, or an institutional investor holding apparel-category assets.
Corporate.industrySummary: Apparel has consolidated under a small number of large multi-brand operators (PVH, VF Corporation, Tapestry, Capri Holdings). The opening underneath is for a regional mid-tier multi-brand operator with deep supply-chain operations and the procurement-grade reliability department stores and institutional investors require.
Corporate.competitorLandscape: PVH Corp (pvh.com) is the multi-brand apparel reference. VF Corporation (vfc.com) holds the multi-brand peer slot. Tapestry Inc (tapestry.com) sits in the multi-brand luxury-accessible peer position. Capri Holdings (capriholdings.com) plays the multi-brand luxury peer reference. We belong in the regional mid-tier multi-brand apparel operator category.
Corporate.positioningStatement: Eastwell Apparel Holdings is a regional multi-brand apparel operator running shared supply chain, retail distribution, and e-commerce infrastructure across a portfolio of brands.
Corporate.positioningRationale: We compete on shared supply-chain depth, retail relationships, and the procurement-grade reliability brand founders and institutional investors need.

targetAudience.primary: Apparel brand founders considering sale, department store buyers seeking single-vendor brand relationships, and institutional investors holding apparel-category assets.
behaviors: Review brand unit economics and category velocity.
Negotiate multi-year retail and supply agreements.
Care about supply-chain efficiency, lead times, and brand-team retention.
Renew on multi-year operating terms.
motivations: Need an operator with shared supply chain.
Need to keep brand identity post-acquisition.
Need a single-vendor multi-brand apparel relationship.

dos: Lead with brand portfolio, supply-chain footprint, and retail relationships.
Speak the language of brand founders, retail buyers, and procurement.
Publish quarterly operator letters.
Refer to brands by name, not by Eastwell tagging.
donts: No social media at the parent level.
No brand consolidation announcements without partner alignment.

messagingPillars.name: Multi-brand operator
messagingPillars.description: We own and partner with four to eight apparel brands across casual, denim, outerwear, and footwear categories. Each retains its identity.

messagingPillars.name: Shared global supply chain
messagingPillars.description: Centralized supply-chain operations across owned and partner factories globally. Brands share sourcing, manufacturing, and logistics under a single operations team.

messagingPillars.name: Retail-ready
messagingPillars.description: Single-vendor supply arrangements with department stores and specialty retailers. Compliance, packaging, and EDI handled in-house.

Corporate.logoDirection: A serif wordmark — Eastwell set in a traditional book serif, with 'Apparel Holdings' beneath in tracked small caps. Used in contracts and the corporate office. Not used on consumer-facing brands.

typography.primary: A traditional book serif for the wordmark and corporate letters.
typography.secondary: A clean enterprise grotesque for operational reports and supply-chain documentation.

Creative.tagline: Clothes for everything but the runway.
Creative.brandNameRationale: Outwearers is a coined plural noun — those who wear the clothes outside the fashion calendar. Single coined word follows the creative-DTC fashion school (Aritzia, Allbirds in coined-word register).
Creative.manifesto: Most fashion brands chase the season. New season, new drop, new sale on the old season. We made Off Season because the rhythm of fashion is exhausting and the clothes are mostly the same. Buy when you want. Wear what holds up. The season is a marketing exercise.
Creative.industrySummary: Fashion has been organized around four seasons for a hundred years. The customer is over it. There's room for a brand that ignores the calendar, releases when the work is done, and treats every garment as the off-season version of itself.
Creative.competitorLandscape: Online Ceramics (onlineceramics.com) does the merch-as-brand thing well. Aimé Leon Dore (aimeleondore.com) has the cultural side. Story Mfg (storymfg.com) holds the slow-craft Creative position. We are sharper and louder than Story Mfg, less merch-y than the others.
Creative.positioningStatement: A fashion brand that releases when the work is done, not when the season says.

targetAudience.primary: 25 to 40. Buys clothes from a small number of brands. Hates being told there's a sale ending. Wears the brand without thinking about it.

dos: Make jokes about the fashion calendar
Tell the customer when not to buy
Photograph the clothes on people who actually wear them
donts: Photograph the clothes against marble or white

Creative.logoDirection: A wordmark in a punchy display serif with the F in OFF stylized as a strike-through, suggesting that this is the version that doesn't follow the rules. Standalone strikethrough-F icon for hangtags, stickers, and social profiles.

typography.primary: Migra for the wordmark and headlines
typography.secondary: PP Neue Montreal for body and hangtag info
typography.rationale: Migra has personality and warmth. Neue Montreal keeps the practical bits readable. The pair feels designed and a little weird.

customSections.title: What it isn't
customSections.body: Not a seasonal brand. Not a sale brand. Not a luxury brand pretending to be quiet. Not too cool to make a joke about itself.

customSections.title: Where it lives
customSections.body: Hangtags with the worst quote from the customer review on them. Stickers in every order. A merch line of two tees and one hoodie, always available. A pop-up shop once a year in a city the brand doesn't ship to.

Creative.brandDescription: A fashion brand that releases when the work is done, not when the season says.
Creative.mission: To build a fashion brand that releases when the work is done, not when the season says.
Creative.vision: The season is a marketing exercise.
coreValues: Confident — we stand behind the work, not the marketing.
Warm — we are friendly, not formal.
Sharp — precision is a form of kindness.
Direct — we say what we mean without softening it.
Playful — seriousness is overrated.
Creative.scope:
Outwearers delivers by:
• Make jokes about the fashion calendar
• Tell the customer when not to buy
• Photograph the clothes on people who actually wear them

Creative.tagline: A small label for considered closets.
Creative.brandNameRationale: Stitchwork is a compound trade word for visible decorative stitching — a real garment-making term. & Co. follows the small-label fashion convention (Pendleton & Co spirit).
Creative.manifesto: We started because everyone we know dresses worse than they could. Not for lack of taste, for lack of nerve. They own one good shirt and wear the bad one. They have a great coat at the back of the closet because they are saving it. We made Stitchwork & Co. to take the saving-it out. Wear the coat. Wear the shirt. The occasion is Tuesday.
Creative.industrySummary: Fashion content is full of inspiration and empty of instruction. Customers do not need another mood board. They need a brand that points at one piece and says wear this, today, with what you already own. There is a real opening for a brand built around the imperative.
Creative.competitorLandscape: Permanent Style (permanentstyle.com) holds the menswear instructional position with a heavier tone. Blackbird Spyplane (blackbirdspyplane.com) owns the recommendation voice. Throwing Fits (the podcast) does the loud opinion. We sit between the instructional and the loud, with our own clothes attached.
Creative.positioning: DRESS BETTER is a clothing brand that talks like a friend with stronger opinions than you. We sell a small collection of upgrade pieces and a weekly note telling you which one to put on.
Creative.targetAudience: Adults 25 to 45 who have an okay wardrobe and a quiet suspicion they could do better. They have the budget, they do not have the time to figure it out, and they want someone to just tell them.
Creative.personality: Bossy in a kind way. Confident. A little impatient. The friend who reorganizes your closet uninvited and is mostly right about it.
Creative.voiceAndTone: Instructions, not invitations. 'Wear this shirt with the trousers you wore yesterday.' 'Roll the sleeves once, not twice.' 'Throw out the brown belt.' Short. Specific. Read like a text.

messagingPillars.title: The note
messagingPillars.body: A weekly email called 'Wear this on Wednesday.' One piece, one outfit, one instruction. No story, no scroll. People forward it. That is the only growth channel.

messagingPillars.title: The upgrade
messagingPillars.body: Twelve pieces a year. Each one replaces something most people already own a worse version of. We say what it replaces on the product page.

messagingPillars.title: The clinic
messagingPillars.body: Once a month we open the inbox and answer outfit questions with one-line replies. Screenshots get posted with the customer's permission. The clinic is the brand.

Creative.logoDirection: Stitchwork & Co. set in a chunky display sans, all caps, slightly condensed, almost looking like a road sign. Used at large scale on packaging and email headers. The mark is a command.
Creative.colorPalette: Marker red #E11A1A as the headline color. Notebook cream #F4EFE3 as the page. Ink #181818 for type. Reads like a handwritten note someone slapped on the fridge.
Creative.typography: One display sans for the instructions. One quiet serif for the product names. Body type left-aligned and short. Never centered.
Creative.brandDescription: We started because everyone we know dresses worse than they could.
Creative.mission: We started because everyone we know dresses worse than they could. Not for lack of taste, for lack of nerve.
Creative.vision: There is a real opening for a brand built around the imperative.

Creative.tagline: A fashion brand for the shapes people actually have.
Creative.brandDescription: The Mannequin Co is a creative-led fashion brand designing every garment from custom mannequins built from real customer body scans rather than standard size grading.
Creative.scope:
The Mannequin Co works across:
• Garment design from custom mannequins based on real customer body scans
• Extended size grading with custom mannequins per size
• Quarterly published essays on body-shape diversity and garment construction
• Customer body-scan service for repeat customers
• Annual customer letter on fit and construction
Creative.mission: To design garments from the body shapes people actually have rather than from idealized size charts.
Creative.vision: A fashion brand whose grading method becomes a standard reference for body-inclusive construction.
coreValues: Specific — every size has its own mannequin.
Considered — body data shapes the garment.
Warm — every body is the customer.
Literary — the writing about construction is part of the brand.
Creative.brandNameRationale: The Mannequin is the foundational garment-construction object — the dress form on which patterns are drafted and garments fitted. The definite article + Co suffix follows the considered-creative trade-name school. The brand stakes a clear creative position on the construction tool that shapes every garment.
Creative.manifesto: Most fashion brands grade sizes from a single mannequin scaled up and down. We started The Mannequin Co because the actual shapes of customer bodies are not scaled versions of a single ideal. We build custom mannequins from real customer body scans and design garments from those mannequins. The grading method is the brand.
Creative.industrySummary: Size grading in fashion is built on idealized mannequins scaled by simple ratios. There is real space for a creative-led brand that explicitly positions on a different grading method — custom mannequins per size, based on real body data.
Creative.competitorLandscape: Universal Standard (universalstandard.com) plays the closest peer in inclusive sizing fashion. Eileen Fisher (eileenfisher.com) holds the considered-modern inclusive peer slot. Mara Hoffman (marahoffman.com) sits in the considered-modern inclusive peer position. Adept (adept.com) plays the body-positive peer reference. We sit alongside Universal Standard with a sharper construction-method creative position.
Creative.positioningStatement: The Mannequin Co is a fashion brand designing every garment from custom mannequins built from real customer body scans, with extended grading per real body data.
Creative.positioningRationale: The brand competes on the construction-method premise. Every garment, every grading decision, and every published essay is built around the custom-mannequin approach.

targetAudience.primary: Fashion buyers 28-55 who have struggled with standard sizing fit and want garments designed from real body shapes.
behaviors: Have difficulty finding well-fitting garments in standard sizing.
Care about construction quality and fit detail.
Buy fewer garments at higher price points when fit is right.
Want a brand that explicitly considers diverse body shapes.
motivations: Want garments designed from real body data.
Want extended grading based on real shapes.
Want a brand with a clear construction philosophy.

dos: Publish the construction method and grading approach on the home page.
Show garments worn on customers of varied body shapes.
Publish the quarterly essay on body-shape diversity and garment construction.
Sign correspondence by the head pattern-maker.
donts: No size-charts that hide the construction approach.

messagingPillars.name: Custom mannequins per size
messagingPillars.description: Every size in the catalog is built from a custom mannequin based on real customer body scan data. The mannequins are documented and published.

messagingPillars.name: Customer body scans
messagingPillars.description: Repeat customers can have their body scanned and stored; subsequent garments are graded against their specific scan.

messagingPillars.name: Quarterly essay
messagingPillars.description: The brand publishes a long-form essay on body-shape diversity and garment construction every quarter. The essay is the brand's primary marketing artefact.

Creative.logoDirection: A wordmark — The Mannequin Co set in a quiet display serif with a small illustration of a dress form beside it. The mark appears on garment labels and the brand's correspondence.

colorPalette.name: Linen
colorPalette.meaning: Primary — the colour of the unbleached muslin used in fittings.

colorPalette.name: Wood
colorPalette.meaning: Secondary — the colour of the dress-form base.

typography.primary: A quiet display serif for the wordmark and the quarterly essay.
typography.secondary: A book serif for construction notes and customer correspondence.
typography.rationale: Two related serifs. The brand reads like a small printed publication on garment construction.
